newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Guilder rates steady in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Guilder rates steady in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Dutch money rates stayed pinned to Thursday's levels in becalmed trade on Friday as the market wound down ahead of the festive season.
"It's been very quiet across the board," one dealer said. "Most players have closed their books for the year."
Call rates were relatively unmoved, with the bulk of deals being done at 2.88 percent, dealers said.
Some dealers said Friday's special advances allocation appeared a little tight, but this was contradicted by others.
The central bank said earlier it allocated 4.76 billion guilders to the market at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent.
Subscriptions up to five billion guilders were met for 15 percent, with no awards above that figure, it said.
The new pact took effect today and runs until December 18.
The guilder was quoting at 112.18 per 100 marks, up a touch from Thursday's 112.195 fixing.
